newsitem.title: POLAND: Pilgrims arrive for Eucharistic congress in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Pilgrims arrive for Eucharistic congress in Poland.

text.p: The first of an expected one million pilgrims began gathering in the western Polish city of Wroclaw on Sunday for a world gathering of Roman Catholics which will culminate in a visit by Pope John Paul on May 31.

At an opening ceremony, Wroclaw Archbishop Henryk Gulbinowicz welcomed guests of various faiths, Catholic clergy and lay people from 86 countries who will attend lectures, seminars and religious services during the week-long event.

The 46th International Eucharistic Congress is the first to be held in Eastern Europe eight years after the overthrow of communist regimes and it will consider how to build a better world based on love of God and mankind, Polish television said.
"May the people of the waning 20th century look at this congress and say, as pagans did in the early centuries of Christianity: 'Look how they love one another'," Gulbinowicz said.

Speaking in the city's renovated Hitler-era People's Hall, the cardinal said Wroclaw, not far from the German and Czech borders, could become an international gathering place which he likened to "the Strasbourg of Central Europe."
Wroclaw, a city of 645,000, was among formerly German-ruled areas ceded to Poland after the World War Two.
The Polish-born pope will spend two days of his fifth and longest-ever 11-day pilgrimage to his homeland at the congress.

The congress was taking place against the backdrop of a tug-of-war between Poland's secular-minded leftists and liberals, who regard the Church's influence as excessive, and right-leaning pro-Catholic groups.
Arenas of the dispute included Sunday's nationwide referendum to decide the fate of a draft constitution, which many Catholics oppose, and September's parliamentary elections.

The autumn vote is expected to be largely a contest between the co-ruling ex-communists and allied right-wing parties led by the Solidarity trade-union movement who have run neck in neck in the opinion polls for months.
